explanation: Compared against WOWII 59 (Wayback all.html, status O; defs 41, 42, 15): for simple connected G, f(G) ≥ CEIL[sqrt(res(G)·b(G))], with f the largest induced forest, res the Havel–Hakimi residue, and b the largest induced bipartite subgraph. The statement negates the universal claim over connected nontrivial finite graphs, using largestInducedForestSize, residue, and b = largestInducedBipartiteSubgraphSize. The docstring's counterexamples are arithmetically consistent: 101·122 = 111² + 1, so the bound is 112 > 111; and ⌈√170⌉ = 14 > 13. Formal proofs are linked. Faithful.
